indicators.flag: A customer, especially a customer who presented a Chinese passport as identification during the onboarding process, regularly receives funds that are not commensurate with the reported occupation or income, and the source of the funds cannot be attributed to payroll or other legitimate sources of income (i.e., unexplained wealth).
indicators.red_flag: Inbound funds inconsistent with stated occupation/income — unexplained wealth (Chinese-passport onboarding)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a personal account whose inflow volume or wealth velocity is inconsistent with the customer's declared income, occupation, or stated source of funds, escalating when large credits lack a plausible origin for the customer's profile.

build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: During the onboarding process, a customer presents a Chinese passport and a visa that contain the same photograph despite being allegedly issued years apart.
indicators.red_flag: Identity-document photo reuse across separately-issued passport and visa (synthetic/altered ID)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D9 (Identity-verification, document & device/session telemetry), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer, especially a Chinese national, creates an account at a financial institution and reports their occupation as a student during the onboarding process.  This customer then regularly deposits cash into their account or receives wire transfers notated as “tuition” or “living expenses” that are not commensurate with the reported information.  After receiving the funds, the customer may subsequently initiate wire transfers or P2P transactions to unknown individuals who are unrelated to the purpose of the wire transfers or may make credit or debit card payments.
indicators.red_flag: Student account funded as "tuition"/"living expenses" → receive-and-forward to no-relationship payees (mule pass-through)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C2 (Rapid pass-through / flow-through (receive-and-forward) detection).

indicators.flag: A customer, especially a Chinese national, reports their occupation during customer onboarding as a student, retiree, housewife, or other low-income occupation but has unexplained wealth.
indicators.red_flag: Low-income occupation (student/retiree/housewife) vs unexplained wealth mismatch
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer, especially a Chinese national with unexplained wealth, initiates a wire transfer related to a real estate purchase or purchases cashier’s checks made payable to a real estate company.  The customer may be accompanied by a real estate agent at the time of purchasing the cashier’s checks.
indicators.red_flag: Unexplained-wealth customer funds real-estate purchase via wire / cashier's checks to realty company
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D18 (Real-estate / property & valuation data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer, especially a Chinese national, regularly deposits large volumes of cash or cashier’s checks, or receives multiple wire, ACH, or P2P transfers for no business or apparent lawful purpose.  The customer then subsequently uses the funds to purchase a cashier’s check or disperses the funds to other individuals using P2P and wire transfers, often to other high-risk jurisdictions.
indicators.red_flag: Cash / multi-channel inflow → disperse via cashier's check, P2P, wire to high-risk corridors (mule pass-through)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C2 (Rapid pass-through / flow-through (receive-and-forward) detection).

indicators.flag: A customer’s account, especially a Chinese national, receives numerous transfers or deposits, and has a significant number of withdrawals or transfers, none of which appear to be related to routine payroll, living expenses, or customer’s stated expected activity.
indicators.red_flag: High in/out transfer churn unrelated to stated expected activity (flow-through)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C2 (Rapid pass-through / flow-through (receive-and-forward) detection).

indicators.flag: A customer, especially a Chinese national, has large amounts of cash funding cashier’s checks, which are then deposited at another financial institution.
indicators.red_flag: Cash-funded cashier's checks redeposited at a second institution (cash placement layering)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C5 (Cash-intensity / cash-placement anomaly detection); data D2.

indicators.flag: A customer, especially a Chinese national, is reluctant or refuses to provide information regarding the source of funds deposited or transferred into their account or acts evasive when questioned about the purpose of a transaction or may explain it as repayment of a loan.
indicators.red_flag: Customer evasive on source-of-funds / "loan repayment" cover story (KYC non-cooperation)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a customer whose KYC record shows integrity gaps or non-cooperation â overdue EDD documents, refused or evasive responses to information requests, or unresolved inconsistencies â escalating when cooperation failures persist past defined deadlines.
build_logic.source: case-management / KYC remediation system + customer correspondence log
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â AML analyst review & EDD gate

indicators.flag: A customer that is a U.S.-based escrow company receives funds from an unaffiliated, foreign-based shell company or entity in a disparate line of business that are used to purchase real estate in the United States.
indicators.red_flag: Escrow account funded by unaffiliated foreign shell in disparate line of business → US real estate
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.red_flag: Online-marketplace revenue with no inventory-purchase activity (revenue-vs-operations anomaly)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D1 (Core transaction monitoring (deposit/account ledger)), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a business account whose transaction inflows are disproportionate to its declared revenue, headcount, payroll, or operating-expense footprint relative to industry peers, escalating when revenue appears decoupled from any observable operational activity.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared profile and peer cohort
build_logic.source: business deposit ledger joined to KYC business profile + industry peer benchmarks
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: A business owned by a Chinese national regularly receives wire transfers indicating the export of goods to foreign countries including Mexico, China, Hong Kong, and the United Arab Emirates, but rarely, or never, engages in transactions that indicate the purchase of goods to maintain inventory.
indicators.red_flag: Export-receipt wires without matching inventory procurement (TBML documentary mismatch)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C22 (Trade-based money-laundering & documentary anomaly detection); data D15.

indicators.flag: A small U.S.-based business in the electronics or real estate industry receives wires from Mexico, China, Hong Kong, and the United Arab Emirates and has no known nexus to these countries.
indicators.red_flag: Small business receives wires from high-risk corridors with no business nexus
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.flag: A customer, especially a Chinese national, regularly receives P2P or wire transfers from unknown individuals and subsequently uses those funds to make a substantial credit card payment.  If questioned about the source of the funds, the customer may state that the transfers are from U.S.-based family members of Chinese citizens who are sending the customer funds to purchase goods.
indicators.red_flag: Inbound P2P/wire from unknown parties → large credit-card paydown (third-party card-payment funnel)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C3 (Multi-originator funnel-in / fan-out network detection).

indicators.flag: A customer, especially a Chinese national, regularly uses a credit card to purchase large volumes of electronics or other luxury goods.
indicators.red_flag: High-volume card spend on electronics / luxury goods (trade-good acquisition spend)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D4 (Card & merchant-category (MCC) transaction data), not currently held → source data first.
